transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?
What scared me enough to come in is that I’ve started thinking it might be simpler if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow. I don’t have any plan to hurt myself, but those thoughts have been unsettling.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or sad most of the day recently?

Yes, most days. It feels like there’s a gray film over everything, even simple things like making tea or looking out at my garden. There’s just this quiet heaviness I can’t seem to talk myself out of.
About how long have you been feeling this heaviness?
About eight months now. It started around the time my brother’s health and behavior changed so suddenly.
Have you ever had periods lasting several days where you felt unusually energized, wired, or didn't need much sleep, which was very different from your normal self?
No, I can’t say I’ve had anything like that.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling down or depressed like this before in your life?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time that felt quite like this.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?
Yes. I still take out my watercolor supplies sometimes, but then I just sit looking at the paper and put them away. The pleasure I used to get from the colors and light just isn’t there.
How has your sleep been lately?
I fall asleep unevenly, and then I often wake up around three or four. My mind starts going over phone calls, forms, whether I handled things correctly. By morning, it feels like I’ve hardly rested.
